FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( Part 2 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 22 April 1990 } after 
the draft finalized by the Inland and Harbour Craft Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Transport Engineering Division Council. 

This standard lays down the requirements for fair leads and is being issued in the following two parts; 

Part 1 Two-lip fair leads 
Part 2 Roller fairleads 

While preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from ISO 412'7/2-1980 'Shipbuilding — 
Inland vessels — Fairleads Part 2 Roller fan leads 1 , issued by the International Organization for 
Standardization ( ISO ).

IS 13004 ( Part 2 ) t 1990 



Indian Standard 



INLAND VESSELS — FAIRLEADS — 
SPECIFICATION 



PARTS ROLLER FAIRLEADS 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard lays down the requirements 
for roller fair leads for inland vessels. 

2 CLASSIFICATION 

2.1 This standard specifies the following two 
types of fairlcads: 

a) Type Z — Common roller fairlead. 

b) Type R — Fairlead with a collapsible 

roller. 

3 DIMENSIONS 

3.1 The dimensions of the fairlead shall be as 
given in Tables 1 and 2. 

4 MATERIAL 

4.1 The components of fairleads shall be made 
from the following material meeting the require- 
ments shown against each: 

Components Material 



Body 



Roller 



Weldable steel having a 
yield point of 250 N/mm s 
( ^ 25 kgf/mma ). 

Cast steel, or malleable 
cast iron having a yield 
point of 40 Njmm 1 
( ;= 24kgf/mm 3 ). 



Components 
Bolt and Axle 

Bush 



Material 

Steel having a yield point 
of 360 N/mma ( ~ 36 kgf/ 
mm 3 ). 

Bronze 



5 MANUFACTURE, WORKMANSHIP AND 
FINISH 

5.1 The construction of roller fairleads and 
the method of welding parts shall be such as 
to meet the requirements laid down in the 
standard. 

5.2 The body shall be welded, with blunted 
edges and polished welds. 

5.3 The rollers shall be clean castings, with 
smooth working surfaces. 

6 PACKING 

6.1 The fairleads shall be suitably packed in 
accordance with the best prevalent trade 
practices. 

7 MARKING 

7.1 The fairleads shall be suitably marked with 
the nominal size and the indication of the 
source of manufacture.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards 
Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products 
covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance: that they have been produced to comply 
with the requirements of that standard under a we] I denned system of inspection, testing and 
quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard 
marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a 
further safeguard Deiails of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark 
may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau ol 
Indian Standards. 



.a of Indian Standard* 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goodi 
and attending to connected matters in the country.

without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the fr^c use, in the course of 
implementing the uandard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations.
